references.text: Jesus speaks of a "baptism" he must undergo – a metaphor for the suffering and death he faces. The word "baptism" (βάπτισμα) is used here figuratively to describe being overwhelmed by suffering, and Jesus expresses an intense inner tension (συνέχομαι) until this is completed.

In [ref:Mark 10:38-39|Mark 10:38-39], Jesus uses the same image of baptism when he asks James and John if they can be "baptized with the baptism I am baptized with," linking it directly to his impending suffering.
[ref:Matt 20:22-23|Matt 20:22-23] is the parallel to the Mark passage, where Jesus again refers to his suffering as a "baptism" that the disciples will also have to undergo.
[ref:Isa 53:3-5|Isaiah 53:3-5] describes the suffering servant who was crushed for our transgressions – the suffering Jesus here looks forward to as his "baptism."
In [ref:Ps 42:8|Psalm 42:8], it is said that God's waves and billows pass over the psalmist – an image of overwhelming suffering that corresponds with the baptism metaphor in Luke 12:50.
[ref:Ps 69:2-3|Psalm 69:2-3] describes sinking into deep waters, where the water reaches up to the neck – a prophetic parallel to Jesus' image of being "baptized" in suffering.
In [ref:Luke 18:31-33|Luke 18:31-33], Jesus concretely predicts the suffering he refers to figuratively as "baptism" in 12:50 – that he will be handed over, mocked, mistreated, and killed.
[ref:Luke 22:44|Luke 22:44] shows the intense inner anguish Jesus experienced in Gethsemane, which reflects what he expressed with the words "I am constrained" (συνέχομαι) in 12:50.
In [ref:John 12:27-28|John 12:27-28], Jesus expresses a similar inner tension before his suffering: "Now my soul is troubled," but he chooses to complete the task the Father has sent him to do.
In [ref:Phil 1:23|Philippians 1:23], Paul uses the same Greek word συνέχομαι to describe being "pressed on both sides," reflecting the inner tension Jesus describes in Luke 12:50.

[ref:Isa 43:2|Isaiah 43:2] promises that God will be with his people when they pass through waters and rivers – an image that sheds light on Jesus' certainty that he will come through his "baptism" of suffering.
